Examples.Title: Send a follow-up or steer
Examples.Description:
Send a follow-up prompt to an existing active agent. Without
`delivery`, the prompt starts a new run that uses the agent's
current conversation and workspace state, and only one run can
be active per agent at a time. With `delivery: steer`, the
agent's running turn takes the prompt when it can, and otherwise
the prompt becomes the agent's next follow-up. On success, a
steer returns `202` with no run object. `delivery` says what
happened, and a `steered` response can include `runId`.
Examples.Code:
### Send a follow-up or steer
# @name createRun
POST {{host}}/v1/agents/{{id}}/runs
Authorization: Bearer {{token}}
Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json

{
  "prompt": {
    "text": "Also add troubleshooting steps",
    "images": [
      "string"
    ]
  },
  "model": {
    "id": "composer-2",
    "params": [
      {}
    ]
  },
  "mcpServers": [
    {
      "name": "github",
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"
      ],
      "env": {
        "GITHUB_TOKEN": "ghp_..."
      }
    }
  ],
  "envVars": {},
  "mode": "agent"
}

## Responses
# 201
# Description: Run created and enqueued. Returned for a request without `delivery`.
# Content-Type: application/json
# 202
# Description: Steer accepted. Returned for `delivery` set to `steer`.
# Content-Type: application/json
# 400
# Description: Validation error or malformed request body. Steering adds two `validation_error` cases, a steer body with any top-level field besides `prompt` and `delivery` or a `delivery` other than `steer`, and a steer that Cursor refuses. For extra fields on a steer, the message names them, such as `"model" is not allowed with delivery "steer"` or `"model", "mode" are not allowed with delivery "steer"`. Cursor checks the body before it checks whether steering is available. A follow-up or steer to a subagent that only its parent agent can drive also returns `validation_error`, with the message "Follow-ups and steers to subagents are not supported. Send them to the parent agent."
# Content-Type: application/json
# 401
# Description: Invalid, missing, or unsupported API key. When the API key fails authentication, the body has a top-level `code` and `message` instead of an `error` object.
# Content-Type: application/json
# 403
# Description: Authenticated but insufficient permissions, plan required, or feature unavailable (`feature_unavailable`), including a steer when steering isn't available for your account.
# Content-Type: application/json
# 404
# Description: Resource not found.
# Content-Type: application/json
# 409
# Description: The agent already has an active run and the request has no `delivery` (`agent_busy`), or the agent is archived (`agent_archived`).
# Content-Type: application/json
# 429
# Description: Rate limit exceeded. Response includes `Retry-After`, `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset` headers.
# Content-Type: application/json
# 500
# Description: Internal server error.
# Content-Type: application/json

Examples.Title: Create A User-Scoped Worker Token
Examples.Description:
Create a one-hour user-scoped token for a My Machines worker to run as an
active team member. Requires an agent-scoped team service account
API key. User-scoped tokens can't mint other user-scoped tokens.
Examples.Setup: This example assumes `using CursorAgents;` is in scope and `apiKey` contains the required credential.

Examples.Title: Stream a run
Examples.Description:
Stream Server-Sent Events for one run. Event types are
`status`, `assistant`, `thinking`, `tool_call`,
`interaction_update`, `heartbeat`, `result`, `error`, and
`done`.

- `status` carries `{ runId, status }`. It has no `id` line
  and is replayed at the top of every reconnect.
- `result` carries `{ runId, status, text?, durationMs?,
  git? }`; `text` is the final assistant reply, `durationMs`
  the wall-clock duration, and `git` mirrors `Run.git`.
- `interaction_update` carries the richer SDK-shape update
  used by the TypeScript SDK and is emitted alongside the
  simplified events that share the same event id. Use this if
  you want the full SDK stream; otherwise handle the simplified
  events and ignore it.

Reconnect with the `Last-Event-ID` header to resume after a
disconnect; the event ID must belong to the requested run
otherwise the endpoint returns `400 invalid_last_event_id`.
Responses include the `X-Cursor-Stream-Retention-Seconds`
header; after the retention window the endpoint may return
`410 stream_expired`. `tool_call` event data uses the
`RunStreamToolCallData` schema.
Examples.Code:
### Stream a run
# @name streamRun
GET {{host}}/v1/agents/{{id}}/runs/{{runId}}/stream
Authorization: Bearer {{token}}
Last-Event-ID: {{Last-Event-ID}}
Accept: application/json, text/event-stream

## Responses
# 200
# Description: SSE stream of run events.
# Content-Type: text/event-stream
# 400
# Description: Validation error or malformed request body.
# Content-Type: application/json
# 401
# Description: Invalid, missing, or unsupported API key. When the API key fails authentication, the body has a top-level `code` and `message` instead of an `error` object.
# Content-Type: application/json
# 403
# Description: Authenticated but insufficient permissions, plan required, or feature unavailable.
# Content-Type: application/json
# 404
# Description: Resource not found.
# Content-Type: application/json
# 410
# Description: Stream retention window has elapsed (`stream_expired`).
# Content-Type: application/json
# 429
# Description: Rate limit exceeded. Response includes `Retry-After`, `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset` headers.
# Content-Type: application/json
# 500
# Description: Internal server error.
# Content-Type: application/json
